messages:
jen: Heads up — docs PR #501 (migration guide + SDK snippet) is blocked. Need a quick runtime confirmation on the default for `modelFallbackWindow`. CI preview is failing a reference in the text.
max: Is this the same routing field we set in the runtime config? I remember a 1000ms default at one point.
kai: I think runtime PR 234 bumped it. My notes say 1500ms and changed semantics to a soft timeout (not queue). cc @tom for confirmation.
docs-ci-bot: Preview build finished for PR 501 — https://staging-docs.redwood.ai/pr-501 — failures: linkcheck, examples linting.
jen: Can @tom confirm two things: 1) is the default 1500ms (or something else), and 2) does this window mean we queue requests waiting for primary, or do we immediately route to fallback after the window? Also, how do SDK retries interact?
tom: Confirmed: `modelFallbackWindow` is a per-request routing timeout expressed in milliseconds (default 1500). It is NOT a queue length. Behavior: runtime will wait up to the window for the primary model to become ready/respond; if it doesn’t, the request is routed to the configured fallback model. There is no automatic intra-request retry against the primary after fallback — once routed, the fallback handles the request.
tom: Additional details: the default 1500ms applies to hosted and Private control-plane runtime when no customer override is set. For Dedicated, the customer config overrides it, but if unset runtime defaults to 1500ms. This window is applied within the same capacity tier/region; cross-region fallbacks use separate routing policies and can have different effective latencies.
max: OK — so SDK-level retries (e.g., client retry on network errors) are independent and may cause additional attempts, correct?
tom: Right. SDK retries are orthogonal — the client may re-send the request on network failure according to client retry policy. But the runtime does not perform an extra attempt on the primary once a fallback is chosen for that request.
maria: Suggested docs wording to unblock the PR: "modelFallbackWindow: 1500  # milliseconds. If the primary model does not start producing a response within this window, requests are routed to the fallback model. This is a routing timeout, not a queue length. The runtime will not retry the original request against the primary after a fallback is chosen. SDK-level retries for network errors may still occur independently."
maria: Example config snippet for the migration guide (inline):
```yaml
routing:
  primary: "gpt-neo-2.7b"
  fallback: "gpt-neo-1.3b"
  modelFallbackWindow: 1500
```
jen: LGTM — I'll update the PR text and examples with that snippet and re-run the preview. @docs-ci-bot please kick off a new preview when I push.
docs-ci-bot: Build queued for PR 501 — preview will be available shortly: https://staging-docs.redwood.ai/pr-501/preview-1845
kai: Quick follow-up: for streaming responses, if the fallback emits the first token within the window but the primary starts later, which stream do clients see? I assume the first-to-produce wins. @tom?
tom: Correct — for streaming, the runtime prefers the first model to produce any token and that stream is returned to the client. If the primary begins producing later for that same request, its output is discarded for that request. Add a short sentence in the streaming section to make this explicit.
jen: Perfect, will add that line and re-run. Thanks everyone! :rocket:
